extracted.intended_audience: patent owners, patent attorneys/agents, third-party requesters, and USPTO examiners involved in ex parte or inter partes reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and quality/procedural standards for preparing, presenting, and processing claim amendments, new claims, drawings, fees, replies, and examiner consideration in ex parte and inter partes patent reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for changes to patent claims (showing amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: For changes to the patent claims, one must submit a copy of the entire patent claim with the amendments shown by underlining and single bracketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Amend claim 6 as follows: Claim 6. (amended), The apparatus of claim [5] 1 wherein the [first] second piezoelectric element is parallel to the [second] third piezoelectric element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing dependency of an original claim
rubrics_metrics.description: If the dependency of any original patent claim is to be changed by amendment, it is proper to make that original patent claim dependent upon a later filed higher numbered claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cancellation of entire claim(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Original patent claim canceled — in writing, direct cancellation of the entire patent claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example wording: Cancel claim 6. Also applies to canceling a proposed new claim previously added in the reexamination: Cancel claim 15.

rubrics_metrics.name: Re-presentation of original patent claims (no markup)
rubrics_metrics.description: When re-presenting an original patent claim (i.e., presenting it unchanged), present it with no underlining or bracketing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Amend claim 4 to read as original patent claim 4: Claim 4. The apparatus of claim 1 wherein the first piezoelectric element is perpendicular to the second piezoelectric element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of new claims (formatting)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each proposed new claim (a claim not found in the patent that is newly presented in the reexamination proceeding) should be presented with underlining throughout the claim, including the claim number and status indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Insert new claim 7 as follows: Claim 7 (New). The apparatus of claim 5 further comprising electrodes attaching to said opposite faces of the second and third piezoelectric elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim numbering rules during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Original claim numbering does not change. Added claims are numbered beginning with the next higher number than the number of claims in the original patent. If new claims added and later canceled prior to issuance, the examiner will renumber remaining new claims for the certificate to follow original highest claim number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A claim number previously assigned to a new claim that has been canceled should not be reassigned to a different new claim during the reexamination proceeding. (Example explained in text.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of new claims (presentation and support)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment of a new claim must present the entire text of the new claim containing the amendatory material, and it must be underlined throughout the claim, including the claim number and status indicator. The presentation cannot contain any bracketing or other indication of what was in the previous version of the claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owner must point out what is changed in the “Remarks” portion of the amendment. As per 37 CFR 1.530(e), each change made in the claim must be accompanied by an explanation of the support in the disclosure of the patent (the reexamination specification) for the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of original patent claims more than once (how to show cumulative changes)
rubrics_metrics.description: When more than one amendment to an original patent claim is made, the second amendment must include (1) the changes previously presented in the first amendment as well as (2) the new changes presented in the second amendment. Deletions of words that were added in a prior amendment (and which never appeared in the original patent) are not shown in brackets in subsequent amendments; added words are underlined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrative example: Original Claim 1 A cutting means... First amendment: Claim 1. (amended), A [cutting means] knife having a bone handle... Second amendment: Claim 1. (twice amended), A [cutting means] knife having a handle portion and a serrated blade portion. 'bone' (introduced in first amendment) is simply omitted in the second amendment; 'serrated' (new) is underlined; 'notched' (from first amendment) is deleted without brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of patent expiration during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If the patent expires during an ex parte or inter partes reexamination proceeding and the patent claims have been amended in that reexamination proceeding, the Office will hold the amendments as being improper, and all subsequent reexamination will be on the basis of the unamended patent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendments will be incorporated into the patent by certificate after expiration of the patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-references to related MPEP sections
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific clerical handling rules and related amendment procedures are found in other MPEP sections: e.g., MPEP §2270 (ex parte reexamination clerical handling), §2670 (inter partes reexamination), §2283/§2285 (merged proceedings), and §2295 (pending reexamination where a reexamination certificate has issued).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing amendments in a pending reexamination that follows a prior reexamination certificate or reissue patent, follow the guidance in those referenced sections regarding italics/brackets treatment and presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of patent drawings — sketch for examiner approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Any change to the patent drawings must be submitted as a sketch on a separate paper showing the proposed changes in red for approval by the examiner. Upon approval, only new sheets of drawings including the changes and in compliance with 37 CFR 1.84 must be filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amended figures must be identified as 'Amended,' added figures as 'New,' and canceled figures must be surrounded by brackets and identified as 'Canceled.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on amending original drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the original patent drawing sheets are not permitted; any change must be made by submitting a new sheet of drawings for each sheet changed. The change may NOT be made on the original patent drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annotated Sheet and figure labeling requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner should submit an ink showing of proposed drawing changes on a separate paper clearly labeled 'Annotated Sheet', which will be made part of the record. After approval, sheets of substitute or new drawings must be submitted for each changed sheet. If a new drawing sheet contains multiple figures, each figure must be marked as 'Amended' or 'New' as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not sufficient to generally indicate the entire sheet is amended (e.g., placing 'Amended' only in the header). Each figure's status must be individually identified (example provided where only Figure 2 is amended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing new drawing sheets relative to NIRC (Quayle action SSPs)
rubrics_metrics.description: New sheets of drawings must be entered into the record in the reexamination file prior to preparation of a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC). If proposed drawing correction approved but new sheets not filed and proceeding is otherwise in condition for NIRC, prepare an ex parte Quayle Office action setting an appropriate shortened statutory time period (SSP) for filing the new sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reexamination was requested by a third party requester, set SSP of ONE MONTH or thirty days, whichever is longer. If requested by patent owner, ordered under 35 U.S.C. 257, or Director ordered, set SSP of TWO MONTHS. If new sheets not timely filed, the reexamination certificate will be issued with drawings that do not reflect the proposed changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of inventorship during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: When correct inventors were not named, the Director may, on petition of all parties with satisfactory proof and payment of fee under 37 CFR 1.20(b), include in the reexamination certificate an amendment naming the actual inventor(s). The petition must satisfy 37 CFR 1.324.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a compliant petition is filed and the proceeding concludes other than by a reexamination certificate, a certificate of correction indicating the change of inventorship will be issued upon request by the patentee (37 CFR 1.530(l)(2)). An incorrect inventorship may alternatively be corrected by reissue under 35 U.S.C. 251 (see MPEP §1412.04).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of excess claims fees during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess claims fees apply to excess claims proposed to be added to a patent by their presentation during a reexamination proceeding on or after December 8, 2004, pursuant to 37 CFR 1.20(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The independent claims fee (37 CFR 1.20(c)(3)) is due for each independent claim in excess of three and in excess of the number of independent claims in the patent being reexamined. The total claims fee (37 CFR 1.20(c)(4)) is due for each claim in excess of twenty and in excess of the number of claims in the patent being reexamined. If amendment only revises existing claims and provides no new claim, no claim fee is due.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples illustrating excess claims fee application
rubrics_metrics.description: Concrete examples to illustrate when excess claims fees apply given a patent with six independent claims and thirty total claims:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A) No excess fee if patent owner cancels ten claims (two independent) and adds ten claims (two independent). B) Independent excess fee for a seventh independent claim is due if cancels ten (two independent) and adds ten (three independent). C) Total excess fee for a thirty‑first claim is due if cancels ten (two independent) and adds eleven (two independent). D) Both independent and total excess fees due if cancels ten (two independent) and adds eleven (three independent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of disclaimed or previously canceled claims from fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim disclaimed under 35 U.S.C. 253 and 37 CFR 1.321(a) as of the date of filing of the request for reexamination is not considered to be a claim in the patent for purposes of excess claims fee calculations. The same applies to a claim canceled via a prior Reexamination Certificate, reissue patent, or Certificate of Correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for fee deficiency in excess claims fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If excess claims fees required by 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) are not paid with presentation of the excess claims, a Notice of Defective Paper in Ex Parte Reexamination will be issued to correct the defect (fee deficiency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For third-party requested reexaminations, a one-month time period (PTOL-475) will be set for correction. For patent-owner requested reexaminations or Director ordered reexaminations, a two-month time period (PTO-2311) will be set. Extension of time may be requested under 37 CFR 1.550(c). If unpaid within the time set, prosecution will be terminated under 37 CFR 1.550(e) effecting abandonment. In responses to a final Office action, the examiner should notify the owner of the fee deficiency in the advisory action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee for filing a petition in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.550(i) and 37 CFR 1.20(c)(6), a petition in an ex parte reexamination proceeding must be accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.20(c)(6), except for certain enumerated petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee amounts: $1,940 for a large entity; $970 for a small entity; $485 for a micro entity (available for patent owners only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply by third party requester — timing and content limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A reply to the patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530 may be filed by the ex parte reexamination requester within two months from the date of service of the patent owner's statement. The reply must be served on the patent owner per 37 CFR 1.248. If the patent owner does not file a statement, no reply will be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reply need not be limited to issues raised in the statement; it may include additional prior art and raise any issue appropriate for reexamination. The third party requester may not file any further papers after the reply; further papers will not be considered and will be returned. The patent owner cannot file papers on behalf of the third party requester.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of statements and replies — timeliness and service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to timely file or serve the documents set forth in 37 CFR 1.530 or 1.535 may result in them being refused consideration. No submissions other than the statement and the reply will be considered prior to examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Untimely submissions will ordinarily not be considered and (except certain late papers by patent owner) will be returned. Any paper requiring proof of service filed without it may be denied consideration; Central Reexamination Unit should inquire whether service was made. If no service, paper placed in file but not considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration by examiner — scope and governing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Once reexamination is ordered, any submissions properly filed and served under 37 CFR 1.530 and 1.535 will be considered by the examiner when preparing the first Office action. Examiner consideration of proposed amendments guided by 37 CFR 1.530(d)-(j); consideration of replies guided by 37 CFR 1.535.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a requester's reply raises issues not previously presented, examiner will treat such issues in the Office action if they are within scope of reexamination; issues outside scope treated pursuant to 37 CFR 1.552(c). Handling of new matter referenced to MPEP §2270. The degree of consideration of submitted references depends on how well the filing party explained content and relevance; examiner initials on citation forms do not mean more extensive consideration than noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct of ex parte reexamination proceedings (general rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: After times for filing the statement and reply have expired, reexamination will be conducted according to procedures for initial examination (sections 132 and 133). The patent owner is permitted to propose any amendment and new claims to distinguish the invention from cited prior art, but no proposed amendment or new claim enlarging the scope of a claim will be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All proceedings, including appeals, will be conducted with special dispatch. Ex parte reexamination will result in issuance of an ex parte reexamination certificate under 37 CFR 1.570. The patent owner will be given at least thirty days to respond to any Office action and may include statements and/or proposed amendments or new claims in response to rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time extensions for patent owner and third-party requested reexaminations
rubrics_metrics.description: Time for taking action by patent owner may be extended as provided; any request must specify the period and be accompanied by petition fee under 37 CFR 1.17(g). Requests for extension in third-party requested reexamination must be filed on or before due date and require sufficient cause; not granted absent sufficient cause or for more than reasonable time. For patent-owner requested or Director ordered reexamination, extensions up to two months may be requested within two months of the original due date; longer extensions must be filed on or before due date and may not be granted absent sufficient cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reply or other action must be filed prior to expiration of extension, and cannot be later than maximum statutory period set by statute. See 37 CFR 90.3(c) for appeal time extensions to CAFC or civil action commencement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failure to timely respond (termination and revival)
rubrics_metrics.description: If patent owner fails to file a timely and appropriate response to any Office action or any written statement of an interview required under 37 CFR 1.560(b), the prosecution in the ex parte reexamination proceeding will be a terminated prosecution, and the Director will proceed to issue and publish a certificate concluding the reexamination proceeding under 37 CFR 1.570 in accordance with the last action of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A petition under 37 CFR 1.137 may be filed to revive a prosecution terminated under this paragraph if the delay was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party participation limitations in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Active participation of the ex parte reexamination requester ends with the reply under 37 CFR 1.535; no further submissions by requester will be acknowledged or considered. No third-party submissions will be acknowledged unless in accordance with 37 CFR 1.510 or entered in the patent file prior to the date of the order for reexamination pursuant to 37 CFR 1.525.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions by third parties filed after the date of the order must meet requirements of and will be treated in accordance with 37 CFR 1.501(a). The patent owner may not file papers on behalf of the requester to circumvent rules; such papers prepared by third party and filed by patent owner will not be entered and will be returned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who conducts the reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The examination will ordinarily be conducted by the same patent examiner who made the determination on whether the reexamination request should be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition under 37 CFR 1.515(c) is granted after an examiner's determination that the request did not raise any substantial new question of patentability (SNQ), the reexamination will generally be conducted by another examiner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art patents and printed publications examiner must review
rubrics_metrics.description: Primary source of prior art will be patents and printed publications cited in the request for ex parte reexamination. Examiner must also consider patents and printed publications: (A) cited by another reexamination requester under 37 CFR 1.510/1.915; (B) cited in patent owner's statement under 37 CFR 1.530 or requester's reply under 37 CFR 1.535 if they comply with 37 CFR 1.98; (C) cited by patent owner under duty of disclosure (37 CFR 1.555) in compliance with 1.98; (D) discovered by examiner in searching; (E) of record in the patent file from earlier examination; (F) of record from any 37 CFR 1.501 submission prior to the date of an order if it complies with 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Degree of consideration of submitted documents is normally limited by the degree to which the submitting party explained content and relevance. If references (other than U.S. patents and publications) are not scanned into the Image File Wrapper (IFW), the record statements about them are the full extent of consideration unless parties supply copies. 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2) requires legible copies of specified foreign patents, publications (or the portions causing listing), pending unpublished U.S. application specifications (or causing portion), and other information or portions causing listing.
